concepts.def: Arson attack on the German parliament used as pretext for emergency decrees curtailing civil liberties.
Law granting Hitler power to legislate without the Reichstag for four years.
Purge of the SA leadership and other opponents, including Ernst Röhm.
Antisemitic laws stripping German Jews of citizenship and prohibiting intermarriage.
January 1942 meeting of senior Nazi officials coordinating the 'Final Solution'.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Great Depression, Weimar political fragmentation, fear of communism and conservative elites' miscalculation paved Hitler's path. Appointed Chancellor on 30 January 1933, he exploited the Reichstag Fire and the Enabling Act to neutralise opposition within months.

The process of Gleichschaltung (coordination) brought trade unions, parties and civil society under Nazi control. The SS, Gestapo and concentration camp system silenced dissent, while propaganda under Goebbels mobilised consent. Rearmament breached Versailles and prepared the ground for aggressive expansion.

Germany's invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939 began WWII in Europe. Conquests across the continent and the invasion of the USSR (Operation Barbarossa, June 1941) facilitated genocide: the murder of approximately six million Jews, alongside Roma, disabled people, Soviet POWs and others. Defeat at Stalingrad (1942-43), Kursk (1943) and on the Western Front led to Berlin's fall and Hitler's suicide on 30 April 1945.
